diagnosis.summary: The order-service Lambda is experiencing severe compute degradation. Mean handler duration has risen from 2 ms to 352 ms (176x increase) and p95 end-to-end latency has jumped from 24 ms to 375 ms (roughly 15.6x baseline), while the request rate and error rate remain unchanged.
diagnosis.root_cause: A Lambda execution environment issue in order-service (such as a new deployment with heavier processing, an inefficient dependency, or a runtime bottleneck) is the most likely root cause of the degradation.
evidence: Mean Lambda handler duration rose from 2 ms to 352 ms, a 176x increase
Median end-to-end latency rose from 17 ms to 360 ms, roughly a 21x increase
p95 end-to-end latency rose from 24 ms to 375 ms, approximately 15.6x baseline, crossing the 10x threshold
Error rate remains at 0%, indicating the service is slow but not failing
Request rate is steady at 2.9 rps, ruling out a traffic spike as the cause
recommended_actions: Review recent order-service Lambda deployments or configuration changes that may have introduced heavier processing logic
Check order-service CloudWatch logs for slow operations, increased cold starts, or SDK initialization delays
Profile the order-service Lambda handler to identify which code path is adding approximately 350 ms of execution time
If a faulty deployment is identified, roll back the order-service Lambda to the last known good version
Consider enabling Lambda Provisioned Concurrency for order-service if cold starts are contributing to the latency increase
